title: What a Process Is
summary: A process is a running program's container - a private address space, a table of handles, a security token, one or more threads and an exit code. Process IDs and handles, why processes cannot see each other's memory, and why that isolation is the reason inter-process communication needs special tools.

cards.q: Why can two processes not share data by writing to the same address?
cards.a: Each has its own private address space; the same address refers to different memory in each.

cards.q: Why is holding a process handle better than remembering its PID?
cards.a: The PID can be reused by another process once the original ends; a handle keeps referring to the same process object.

cards.q: Name four ways processes on one machine can exchange data or signals.
cards.a: Any four of: pipes, file mappings (shared memory), sockets, named events, mutexes and semaphores, window messages, files.

cards.q: What happens to a pipe when the process at its other end crashes?
cards.a: Windows closes that process's handles, so the pipe is closed and the next read or write fails.
